claim: Drosophila melanogaster females shorten the ejaculate holding period (EHP) when incubated with males or mated females shortly after the first mating.
source: In this study, we found that Drosophila melanogaster females shortens the EHP when incubated with males or mated females shortly after the first mating.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations described in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 1.

claim: Male-induced EHP shortening (MIES) requires Or47b+ olfactory neurons.
source: This phenomenon, which we termed male-induced EHP shortening (MIES), requires Or47b+ olfactory and ppk23+ gustatory neurons, activated by 2-methyltetracosane and 7-tricosene, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Male-induced EHP shortening (MIES) requires ppk23+ gustatory neurons.
source: This phenomenon, which we termed male-induced EHP shortening (MIES), requires Or47b+ olfactory and ppk23+ gustatory neurons, activated by 2-methyltetracosane and 7-tricosene, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: 2-methyltetracosane activates Or47b+ olfactory neurons.
source: This phenomenon, which we termed male-induced EHP shortening (MIES), requires Or47b+ olfactory and ppk23+ gustatory neurons, activated by 2-methyltetracosane and 7-tricosene, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral and cellular assays shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: 7-tricosene activates ppk23+ gustatory neurons.
source: This phenomenon, which we termed male-induced EHP shortening (MIES), requires Or47b+ olfactory and ppk23+ gustatory neurons, activated by 2-methyltetracosane and 7-tricosene, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral and cellular assays shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: 2-methyltetracosane and 7-tricosene raise cAMP levels in pC1 neurons.
source: These odorants raise cAMP levels in pC1 neurons, responsible for processing male courtship cues and regulating female mating receptivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by CRE-luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 5E and 5F.

claim: pC1 neurons are responsible for processing male courtship cues.
source: These odorants raise cAMP levels in pC1 neurons, responsible for processing male courtship cues and regulating female mating receptivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior literature cited in the manuscript and calcium imaging data in Figure 6B.

claim: pC1 neurons regulate female mating receptivity.
source: These odorants raise cAMP levels in pC1 neurons, responsible for processing male courtship cues and regulating female mating receptivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior literature cited in the manuscript and re-mating assays in Figure 6C.

claim: Elevated cAMP levels in pC1 neurons reduce EHP.
source: Elevated cAMP levels in pC1 neurons reduce EHP and reinstate their responsiveness to male courtship cues, promoting re-mating with faster sperm ejection.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments using PhotoAC shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Elevated cAMP levels in pC1 neurons reinstate their responsiveness to male courtship cues.
source: Elevated cAMP levels in pC1 neurons reduce EHP and reinstate their responsiveness to male courtship cues, promoting re-mating with faster sperm ejection.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Elevated cAMP levels in pC1 neurons promote re-mating with faster sperm ejection.
source: Elevated cAMP levels in pC1 neurons reduce EHP and reinstate their responsiveness to male courtship cues, promoting re-mating with faster sperm ejection.
evidence: This claim is supported by re-mating assays shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The EHP of females incubated with naive males was approximately 30 min shorter than that of females left in isolation after mating.
source: Notably, the EHP of females incubated with naive males was approximately 30 min shorter than that of females left in isolation after mating (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Little difference in EHP was observed between females incubated with virgin females and those isolated after mating.
source: In contrast, little difference in EHP was observed between females incubated with virgin females and those isolated after mating (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Limited illumination had a marginal impact on MIES.
source: To assess the role of the visual signal in MIES, we examined MIES under dim red light conditions and observed that limited illumination had a marginal impact on MIES (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Incubation with decapitated CS males did not result in a reduction in MIES.
source: Next, we examined MIES in post-mating females incubated with decapitated CS males. These males could serve as a source of olfactory or gustatory signals, but not for auditory or visual signals. Again, no reduction in MIES was observed (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Olfactory or gustatory cues are the key signals responsible for MIES.
source: This strongly suggests that olfactory or gustatory cues are the key signals responsible for MIES.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the decapitated male experiment and supported by the Orco mutant data.

claim: Females deficient in the odorant receptor co-receptor (Orco1) did not exhibit MIES.
source: This is further supported by the observation that females deficient in the odorant receptor co-receptor (Orco1) did not exhibit MIES (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Male odorant(s), especially those detected by olfactory receptors (Or), induce MIES.
source: Thus, it is highly likely that male odorant(s), especially those detected by olfactory receptors (Or), induce MIES.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the Orco mutant data and the decapitated male experiment.

claim: Silencing ORNs expressing Or13a, Or19a, Or23a, Or47b, Or65c, Or67d, or Or88a significantly affected MIES.
source: Our results showed that silencing ORNs expressing Or13a, Or19a, Or23a, Or47b, Or65c, Or67d, or Or88a significantly affected MIES (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Silencing Or47b-positive ORNs exhibited almost complete abolition of MIES.
source: We then focused on the analysis of Or47b-positive ORNs (Figure 2A), which, in contrast to the others, exhibited almost complete abolition of MIES when silenced.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Activation of Or47b-positive ORNs with the thermogenetic activator dTRPA1 resulted in a significant EHP shortening, even in the absence of male exposure.
source: Activation of these neurons with the thermogenetic activator dTRPA1 (Hamada et al., 2008) resulted in a significant EHP shortening, even in the absence of male exposure (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Restoring Orco expression in Or47b ORNs in Orco-deficient females restored MIES.
source: Subsequently, we examined whether restoring Orco expression in Or47b ORNs in Orco-deficient females would restore MIES. Our results confirmed that this is indeed the case (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Or47b-deficient females (Or47b2/Or47b3) exhibited a complete absence of MIES.
source: To establish the necessity of the Or47b receptor gene for MIES, we examined Or47b-deficient females (Or47b2/Or47b3) and observed a complete absence of MIES, whereas heterozygous controls exhibited normal MIES (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Heterozygous Or47b controls exhibited normal MIES.
source: To establish the necessity of the Or47b receptor gene for MIES, we examined Or47b-deficient females (Or47b2/Or47b3) and observed a complete absence of MIES, whereas heterozygous controls exhibited normal MIES (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Reintroduction of Or47b expression in Or47b ORNs of Or47b-deficient females almost completely restored MIES.
source: Furthermore, the reintroduction of Or47b expression in Or47b ORNs of Or47b-deficient females almost completely restored MIES (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: MIES depends on the Or47b receptor gene and Or47b-expressing ORNs.
source: Based on these observations, we concluded that MIES depends on the Or47b receptor gene and Or47b-expressing ORNs.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Methyl laurate and palmitoleic acid can activate Or47b ORNs only in the presence of a functional Or47b gene.
source: Previous studies have shown that methyl laurate and palmitoleic acid can activate Or47b ORNs only in the presence of a functional Or47b gene (Dweck et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Methyl laurate and palmitoleic acid did not induce significant EHP shortening, even when applied at concentrations as high as 1440 ng.
source: However, in our investigation, none of these odorants induced significant EHP shortening, even when applied at concentrations as high as 1440 ng (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Incubation with females engineered to produce male oenocytes significantly shortened EHP.
source: Indeed, incubation with females engineered to produce male oenocytes significantly shorten EHP, strongly suggesting that male oenocytes serve as a source for the MIES pheromone.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Incubation with males possessing feminized oenocytes resulted in significant EHP shortening.
source: Unexpectedly, however, incubation with males possessing feminized oenocytes also resulted in significant EHP shortening (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Oenocytes may not be the sole source of the MIES pheromone.
source: This raises the possibility that oenocytes may not be the sole source of the MIES.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that males with feminized oenocytes still induce MIES.

claim: Incubation with males of Drosophila simulans, Drosophila sechellia, and Drosophila erecta induced EHP shortening.
source: We found that incubation with males of other closely related species, such as Drosophila simulans, Drosophila sechellia, and Drosophila erecta, also induced EHP shortening, whereas incubation with Drosophila yakuba males did not (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Incubation with Drosophila yakuba males did not induce EHP shortening.
source: We found that incubation with males of other closely related species, such as Drosophila simulans, Drosophila sechellia, and Drosophila erecta, also induced EHP shortening, whereas incubation with Drosophila yakuba males did not (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: 2MC at 750 ng significantly reduced EHP.
source: Among these, 2MC at 750 ng was the only one that significantly reduced EHP (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: 2MC was mainly found in males, but not in virgin females.
source: 2MC was mainly found in males, but not in virgin females (Dweck et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: 2MC is present in D. melanogaster, D. simulans, D. sechellia, and D. erecta, but not in D. yakuba.
source: Notably, it is present in D. melanogaster, D. simulans, D. sechellia, and D. erecta, but not in D. yakuba (Dweck et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The 2MC-induced EHP shortening was not observed in Orco-deficient females.
source: Moreover, the 2MC-induced EHP shortening was not observed in Orco- or Or47b-deficient females (Figure 3B and C), but was restored when Orco expression was reinstated in Or47b ORNs in Orco-deficient mutants (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The 2MC-induced EHP shortening was not observed in Or47b-deficient females.
source: Moreover, the 2MC-induced EHP shortening was not observed in Orco- or Or47b-deficient females (Figure 3B and C), but was restored when Orco expression was reinstated in Or47b ORNs in Orco-deficient mutants (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 2MC-induced EHP shortening was restored when Orco expression was reinstated in Or47b ORNs in Orco-deficient mutants.
source: Moreover, the 2MC-induced EHP shortening was not observed in Orco- or Or47b-deficient females (Figure 3B and C), but was restored when Orco expression was reinstated in Or47b ORNs in Orco-deficient mutants (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 2MC acts as an odorant ligand for Or47b and shortens the EHP through this receptor.
source: Our behavioral observations strongly suggest that 2MC acts as an odorant ligand for Or47b and shortens the EHP through this receptor.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Incubation with mated females resulted in a significant shortening of EHP.
source: In contrast to incubation with virgin females, incubation with mated females resulted in a significant shortening of EHP (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mated females carry male pheromones, including 7-T and cVA, which are transferred during copulation.
source: Mated females carry male pheromones, including 7-T and cVA, which are transferred during copulation (Laturney and Billeter, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Incubation with a piece of filter paper perfumed with 150 ng of 7-T significantly shortened the EHP.
source: Indeed, our experiments revealed that incubation with a piece of filter paper perfumed with 150 ng of 7-T significantly shortened the EHP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Incubation with cVA did not produce EHP shortening.
source: Conversely, incubation with cVA and 7-pentacosene, a related CHC, did not produce the same effect (Figure 4B and C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Incubation with 7-pentacosene did not produce EHP shortening.
source: Conversely, incubation with cVA and 7-pentacosene, a related CHC, did not produce the same effect (Figure 4B and C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 7-T has been found at levels of 432 ng in males.
source: 7-T has been found at levels of 432 ng in males (Scott and Richmond, 1988), 25 ng in virgin females, and 150 ng in mated females (Laturney and Billeter, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: 7-T has been found at levels of 25 ng in virgin females.
source: 7-T has been found at levels of 432 ng in males (Scott and Richmond, 1988), 25 ng in virgin females, and 150 ng in mated females (Laturney and Billeter, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: 7-T has been found at levels of 150 ng in mated females.
source: 7-T has been found at levels of 432 ng in males (Scott and Richmond, 1988), 25 ng in virgin females, and 150 ng in mated females (Laturney and Billeter, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: ppk23-expressing tarsal neurons sense 7-T and regulate sexual behavior in males and females.
source: Although the receptors for 7-T remain unknown, ppk23-expressing tarsal neurons have been shown to sense these compounds and regulate sexual behavior in males and females (Thistle et al., 2012; Toda et al., 2012; Vijayan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Silencing ppk23 neurons almost completely abolished MIES.
source: Subsequently, we silenced ppk23 neurons, and as a result, MIES was almost completely abolished, underscoring the pivotal role of 7-T in MIES (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: DEG/ENac channel genes expressed in ppk23 neurons, including ppk23 and ppk29, were found to be dispensable for MIES.
source: However, DEG/ENac channel genes expressed in ppk23 neurons, including ppk23 and ppk29, were found to be dispensable for MIES (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: Neither ppk23 deficiency nor ppk28 deficiency recapitulates the sexual behavioral defects caused by silencing ppk23 neurons.
source: This aligns with the previous observations that neither ppk23 deficiency nor ppk28 deficiency recapitulates the sexual behavioral defects caused by silencing ppk23 neurons (Lu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The neuropeptide Dh44 determines the timing of sperm ejection or EHP.
source: The neuropeptide Dh44 determines the timing of sperm ejection or EHP (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Dh44 receptor neurons involved in EHP regulation also express doublesex (dsx).
source: The same study found that Dh44 receptor neurons involved in EHP regulation also express doublesex (dsx), which encodes sexually dimorphic transcription factors.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: pC1 neurons express Dh44 receptors.
source: A recent study has revealed that pC1 neurons, a specific subgroup of dsx-expressing central neurons in the female brain, do indeed express Dh44 receptors (Kim et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The pC1 neurons comprise five distinct subtypes.
source: The pC1 neurons comprise five distinct subtypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior literature and connectome analyses cited in the manuscript.

claim: The pC1a, b, and c subtypes have been implicated in mating receptivity.
source: Of these, the pC1a, b, and c subtypes have been implicated in mating receptivity (Deutsch et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2024), while the remaining pC1d and e subtypes have been implicated in female aggression (Chiu et al., 2023; Deutsch et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The pC1d and e subtypes have been implicated in female aggression.
source: Of these, the pC1a, b, and c subtypes have been implicated in mating receptivity (Deutsch et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2024), while the remaining pC1d and e subtypes have been implicated in female aggression (Chiu et al., 2023; Deutsch et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Silencing of the pC1 subset comprising the pC1a, b, and c subtypes with GtACR1 led to an increase in EHP.
source: Our experiments revealed that silencing of the pC1 subset comprising the pC1a, b, and c subtypes with GtACR1 led to an increase in EHP (Figure 5A), whereas silencing of the pC1d and e subtypes had a limited effect on EHP (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Silencing of the pC1d and e subtypes had a limited effect on EHP.
source: Our experiments revealed that silencing of the pC1 subset comprising the pC1a, b, and c subtypes with GtACR1 led to an increase in EHP (Figure 5A), whereas silencing of the pC1d and e subtypes had a limited effect on EHP (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Silencing pC1a with a subtype-specific split-Gal4 almost completely suppressed mating receptivity.
source: We generated a subtype-specific split-Gal4 for pC1a and found that, as expected, silencing pC1a with this split-Gal4 almost completely suppressed mating receptivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Silencing pC1a alone did not result in increased EHP.
source: However, silencing pC1a alone did not result in increased EHP, suggesting a marginal role of the pC1a subtype in EHP regulation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Concomitant silencing of both pC1b and pC1c neurons significantly increased EHP by 56±6.9 min.
source: In contrast, concomitant silencing of both pC1b and pC1c neurons significantly increased EHP by 56±6.9 min (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: pC1 neurons from virgin females exhibit robust Ca2+ transients in response to male courtship cues, such as the male pheromone cVA and the courtship pulse song.
source: pC1 neurons from virgin females exhibit robust Ca2+ transients in response to male courtship cues, such as the male pheromone cVA and the courtship pulse song (Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: pC1 neurons from mated females display significantly diminished Ca2+ transients.
source: In contrast, those from mated females display significantly diminished Ca2+ transients (Kim et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: When exposed to 2MC or 7-T, pC1b, c neurons exhibited a significant increase in CRE-luciferase activity.
source: Indeed, when exposed to 2MC or 7-T, pC1b, c neurons exhibited a significant increase in CRE-luciferase activity, indicating that these neurons produce higher levels of cAMP in response to these odorants (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CRE-luciferase activity in pC1b, c neurons appeared to peak at specific odorant concentrations that induced significant shortening of the EHP.
source: Notably, CRE-luciferase activity appeared to peak at specific odorant concentrations that induced significant shortening of the EHP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: No evidence of increased CRE-luciferase reporter activity was detected in pC1a, and pC1d and e neurons upon exposure to 2MC or 7-T treatment.
source: In contrast, when we examined other pC1 subsets, such as pC1a, and pC1d and e, we detected no evidence of increased CRE-luciferase reporter activity upon exposure to 2MC or 7-T treatment (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CRE-luciferase reporter activity in the pC1a neurons appears to be dependent on the mating status.
source: Notably, CRE-luciferase reporter activity in the pC1a neurons appears to be dependent on the mating status, as it reaches levels similar to those of pC1b, c neurons in virgin females (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: SAG neurons, which are responsible for relaying SP-dependent mating signals, synapse primarily with the pC1a subtype and to a much lesser extent with other pC1 subtypes.
source: This observation aligns well with connectome data suggesting that SAG neurons, which are responsible for relaying SP-dependent mating signals, synapse primarily with the pC1a subtype and to a much lesser extent with other pC1 subtypes (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Or47b-deficient females showed robust CRE-luciferase activity in response to 7-T, but little activity in response to 2MC.
source: In contrast, Or47b-deficient females showed robust CRE-luciferase activity in response to to 7-T, but little activity in response to 2MC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The odorant receptor Or47b plays an essential role in the selective detection of 2MC.
source: This observation suggests that the odorant receptor Or47b plays an essential role in the selective detection of 2MC (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the Or47b mutant CRE-luciferase data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The induced elevation of cAMP levels in pC1b, c neurons significantly shortened EHP.
source: Indeed, the induced elevation of cAMP levels in pC1b, c neurons significantly shortened EHP, whereas the same treatment applied to pC1a or pC1d and pC1e had no such effect (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Induced elevation of cAMP levels in pC1a or pC1d and pC1e had no effect on EHP.
source: Indeed, the induced elevation of cAMP levels in pC1b, c neurons significantly shortened EHP, whereas the same treatment applied to pC1a or pC1d and pC1e had no such effect (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: pC1b, c neurons play a pivotal role in EHP regulation.
source: This further underscores the pivotal role of pC1b, c neurons in EHP regulation.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the PhotoAC experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Double knockdown of Dh44R1 and Dh44R2 in pC1 neurons seemed to have a limited impact on MIES.
source: However, double knockdown of Dh44R1 and Dh44R2 in pC1 neurons seemed to have a limited impact on MIES (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dh44R signaling in pC1 neurons is not essential for the regulation of EHP or MIES.
source: This suggests that Dh44R signaling in pC1 neurons is not essential for the regulation of EHP or MIES, raising the possibility that other GPCRs may be involved in the upregulation of cAMP levels in pC1 neurons in response to 2MC or 7-T.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the Dh44R knockdown data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Immediately after PhotoAC activation in pC1 neurons, pC1 neurons from freshly mated females became more excitable and exhibited stronger Ca2+ transients in response to cVA.
source: However, immediately after PhotoAC activation in pC1 neurons, pC1 neurons from freshly mated females became more excitable and exhibited stronger Ca2+ transients in response to cVA (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: PhotoAC-induced increase in pC1 excitability is transient and rapidly declines within 10 min.
source: It is important to note that this PhotoAC-induced increase in pC1 excitability is transient and rapidly declines within 10 min (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: PhotoAC activation in pC1b, c neurons substantially increased the re-mating rate compared to the control group.
source: As expected, PhotoAC activation in pC1b, c neurons substantially increased the re-mating rate compared to the control group (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Male odorants that stimulate cAMP elevation in pC1 neurons expedite the removal of the mating plug, consequently leading to increased instances of re-mating.
source: Therefore, we concluded that male odorants that stimulate cAMP elevation in pC1 neurons expedite the removal of the mating plug, consequently leading to increased instances of re-mating (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Sexual plasticity is the ability to modify sexual state or reproductive behavior in response to changing social conditions.
source: Sexual plasticity, the ability to modify sexual state or reproductive behavior in response to changing social conditions, is observed in both vertebrates and invertebrates (Bruce, 1959; Koene and Ter Maat, 2007; Roberts et al., 2012; Steiger et al., 2008; Yagound et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is a definition supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In rodents, exposure to unfamiliar males often leads to the sudden termination of pregnancy, known as the Bruce effect.
source: In rodents, exposure to unfamiliar males often leads to the sudden termination of pregnancy, known as the Bruce effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The Bruce effect is induced by male urinary peptides, such as MHC I peptides, activating the vomeronasal organ.
source: It is induced by male urinary peptides, such as MHC I peptides, activating the vomeronasal organ (Becker and Hurst, 2008; Leinders-Zufall et al., 2004; Zipple et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The Bruce effect enhances reproductive fitness of both sexes, by eliminating the offspring of competing males and enabling females to select better mates even after conception.
source: This effect enhances reproductive fitness of both sexes, by eliminating the offspring of competing males and enabling females to select better mates even after conception.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature and general knowledge about the Bruce effect.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster displays various social behaviors like aggregation, aggression, and sexual behavior.
source: Drosophila melanogaster, the fruit fly, displays various social behaviors like aggregation, aggression, and sexual behavior (Bartelt et al., 1985; Billeter et al., 2006; Billeter and Levine, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Fruit flies primarily use the olfactory system to communicate socially through pheromones.
source: Similar to rodents, they primarily use the olfactory system to communicate socially through pheromones (Kohl et al., 2015; Sengupta and Smith, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: 11-cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA) attracts females but repels males and promotes aggregation.
source: For instance, 11-cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA) attracts females but repels males and promotes aggregation (Billeter and Levine, 2015; Kurtovic et al., 2007; Mane et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: 7-Tricosene (7-T), a cuticular hydrocarbon (CHC) present in males, is an aphrodisiac to females and affects social interactions between males.
source: 7-Tricosene (7-T), a cuticular hydrocarbon (CHC) present in males, is an aphrodisiac to females and affects social interactions between males (Grillet et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: 7,11-heptacosadiene (7,11-HD), a related female-specific pheromone, functions as an aphrodisiac to males, triggering courtship behavior and involving species recognition.
source: On the other hand, 7,11-heptacosadiene (7,11-HD), a related female-specific pheromone, functions as an aphrodisiac to males, triggering courtship behavior and involving species recognition (Antony et al., 1985; Toda et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) in the sensilla of the antennae and maxillary palp are responsible for the detection of long-range volatile pheromones like cVA.
source: Olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) in the sensilla of the antennae and maxillary palp are responsible for the detection of long-range volatile pheromones like cVA, while short-range pheromones like 7-T are sensed by neurons on the forelegs and labellum (Joseph and Carlson, 2015; Kohl et al., 2015; Sengupta and Smith, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Short-range pheromones like 7-T are sensed by neurons on the forelegs and labellum.
